resources.string: Keep microphone capture active while muted

Optional; off by default. Keeps an already verified microphone running while transmission is muted, which may reduce unmute delays and Bluetooth route changes. The Android microphone indicator stays on and battery use may increase. Stop, pause, route loss and network recovery still release capture; it resumes only when unmuted. Applies to the next microphone or duplex connection. This does not guarantee background survival.
Choose before connecting. Echo reduction can help with phone-speaker playback; headphones are still recommended. These options process only the microphone.
Bluetooth microphone processing is managed by Android and the headset. These options are retained for phone or wired/USB input.
Listen to Windows. Send your microphone back.
The selected media output is unavailable. Reconnect it or choose another output. Use Device missing? if Android is hiding a connected Bluetooth device.
The output could not be changed. Choose a connected media output after the current audio setup finishes.
The microphone could not be changed. Check its connection and permissions, and choose a media output before changing to a phone, wired or USB microphone.
Connection order and timeouts apply the next time you connect.
Recovery window: %1$s s · Connection and host controls
Allow Windows to change phone settings

While connected, your paired Windows host can adjust Audio and Advanced preferences, phone volume, media output, desktop audio and microphone mute. Pairing, permissions and microphone consent stay on this phone: Windows can unmute only a microphone this phone turned on in the session. Windows Unmute and Play desktop audio changes last only for this session. A media output change applies right away during playback or duplex with a phone, wired or USB microphone. Other changes apply after Stop and Connect. These controls are unavailable while paused or disconnected.
Copy a report when troubleshooting, or check playback on this phone without connecting to Windows.

Android may show MicDrop only the active Bluetooth device. Open Android\'s output picker, select the device there, then return and choose it in MicDrop to remember it. Your current MicDrop choice stays saved.\n\nFor a headset microphone, enable its Phone calls option in Bluetooth settings if available. A media output does not necessarily support microphone input.
Opening the picker or settings will stop this session. After choosing your device, tap Connect explicitly. Microphone capture will not restart automatically.
The session changed while this dialog was open. Open Device missing? again.
Open Android Bluetooth settings to connect your audio device, then return to MicDrop.

In the Windows app, open Phones → Pair a phone. Scan its QR code or paste the link, tap Connect, then approve the request in Windows. Keep MicDrop open to connect after approval. If you leave the app, tap Reconnect when you return.

Turning this off silences desktop audio while keeping the connection open. Checked means playback is requested; paused means it is temporarily held. Android media output follows the system default between Bluetooth devices. Losing Bluetooth pauses playback on phone-speaker fallback; the microphone keeps its current setting. Tap Use phone speaker for temporary speaker playback. When Bluetooth returns, Android media output resumes automatically. Follow Android media output remains available as a fallback. Choosing a device in the output menu keeps that choice pinned.

Playback follows the selected headset microphone. The media output choice applies after switching to a phone, wired or USB microphone. Turning audio off silences it without changing the headset route.
Desktop audio was not enabled when this session started. Stop, enable audio, and reconnect to add listening.
Turning this off during a microphone session mutes capture. Your choices are remembered; only an explicit Connect starts a new microphone session.
This session started without a microphone. Stop, enable Send microphone, and reconnect to use it.
Choose your microphone input again before connecting.
No stream report yet. Connection details will appear here.
Try %1$s:%2$d with your saved pairing. MicDrop checks the Windows identity before playing and remembers this address only after playback connects.

In the Windows app, open Phones → Pair a phone. Scan its QR code or paste the link, then tap Connect and approve the matching request in Windows. Finding a computer on your network does not pair it automatically.
Scan the entire pairing QR in the Windows app. Back returns to manual entry.
Camera access is only needed for scanning. You can paste the Windows link instead.
Camera unavailable. Paste the Windows link instead.
That QR code is not a valid MicDrop pairing invitation.
That pairing QR expired. Select Pair a phone in Windows and scan the new code.
Scanned Windows at %1$s:%2$d. Tap Connect, then approve the matching request in Windows.
That pairing invitation expired. In the Windows app, open Phones → Pair a phone for a new one.
Pairing window ended, was rejected, or another phone is pending. In the Windows app, open Phones → Pair a phone for a new invitation.
Pairing was not saved. Windows may already have approved the phone; retry the same invitation while it is valid, or select Pair a phone in Windows for a new one.
Pairing cancelled. If Windows already approved this phone, remove it in the Windows app under Phones → Remove selected phone.
Saved connection and phone identity forgotten. Windows may still list the old phone; remove it in the Windows app under Phones → Remove selected phone.
Crash diagnostics copied. Keep this report private.
Playback snapshot copied. Host address and invitation excluded.
Paste the complete Windows pairing or connection link, then tap Connect.
The connection failed. Check the connection status.
Tap Play click in Diagnostics. Stop ends the test.

Tap Play click and listen for the response. This audio-only test uses matching streaming output settings. Tap-to-sound includes touch and scheduling delay; it is not a calibrated latency measurement. Stop, then connect to Windows to include this baseline in the combined log.
Audio is busy. Try again after other playback stops.
